$comment: The native bridge contract, in one file, read by BOTH sides.
Five release blockers in a row were the same bug: the renderer and the Rust
command disagreed about the shape of what crosses `invoke`, and nothing in
CI could see it because headless-Chromium E2E never runs the desktop shell.
Response headers were dropped; `config.params` was dropped; a FormData body
serialised to `{}`; a claim the server sends as a string was declared `i64`.
Each case below is one exact IPC payload.
adapter with the described request and asserts it emits exactly this.
exactly this into the command's argument struct and assert the fields
Drift on either side fails a test instead of shipping.

cases.name: get-with-params
cases.why: A parameterised GET must arrive with its query string. Recovery lost its mandatory `after` and 400d, which is what poisoned every 3.0.0 profile.

cases.name: json-post
cases.why: A JSON body travels as a value, and the caller's deadline travels with it.

cases.name: form-urlencoded-post
cases.why: A non-JSON string body goes on the wire verbatim under its own content type, not wrapped in JSON quotes.

cases.name: binary-response
cases.why: responseType blob/arraybuffer must not be forced through serde_json::Value.

cases.name: multipart-upload
cases.why: Bug 5. A FormData handed to invoke() serialises to {} — it has no enumerable own properties — so every upload arrived as an empty JSON object and 400d.

cases.name: multipart-opaque-blob
cases.why: An encrypted attachment is an unnamed Blob; a browser calls that part "blob" and stamps it application/octet-stream.

cases.name: single-file-upload
cases.why: The attachment path's own command. It shares one multipart implementation with native_multipart so a fix to one is a fix to both.

cases.name: download
cases.why: Attachment download. A multi-megabyte body does not finish inside the 15 s default.

responses.name: headers-are-returned
responses.why: Bug 1. native_fetch returned only status and body, so the operation context compared an absent X-Paracord-History-Epoch against the captured one, called every response a history change, and tore down the realtime stream.

responses.name: non-json-body-is-text
responses.why: Axios leaves an unparseable body on response.data as text. Answering null threw away every plain-text error the server can send.

server_payloads.name: media-token-claims-string-sub
server_payloads.why: Bug 3. The server mints `sub` as a JSON string because a snowflake is past 2^53. The desktop declared it i64 and every native voice join failed with "invalid type: string".

server_payloads.name: media-token-claims-number-sub
server_payloads.why: An older server still sends a bare number; both shapes must read.

secure_store_keys.name: signal-dm-session
secure_store_keys.why: Bug 4. A Signal DM session key is `paracord:signal:session:<64 hex>:<64 hex>` = 153 bytes. A 128-byte cap rejected every one of them, so no encrypted DM could be sent from the desktop.

secure_store_keys.name: unprefixed
secure_store_keys.why: The prefix is the namespace guard and still applies.
